summary: All 112 slide files, four manifests, four concepts records and the extraction log were read, and the recap's substantive course content (L1 mechanics, L2 prompt techniques, L3 harness, L4 pipeline, the four sourced incident case studies, the latency formulas and the 0.8 MB/token figure) traces cleanly to the decks. Five blocking defects sit in the recap's provenance and extraction-limitations sections rather than in its course content: an unsourced '850 occurrences' figure, a cited review-record file that does not exist, 'RAG on Day 4' where slide 27 says 'Up next: Day 4', a claim that the 'Five ideas, one answer' line is unrecoverable when both slide files carry it verbatim, and a reference to a Lecture 3 'slide 24' in a 22-slide deck. The single most important fix is to make §8 and §9 state only what the manifests, concepts records and log actually record.

missing_concepts.concept: Types of models — 'Pick the right kind for the job.'
missing_concepts.source_ref: AAPLecture1_LLM_Foundations slide 12 ('Types of models / Pick the right kind for the job.'); concept record entry 'Types of models', source_reference.slide 12, confidence medium
missing_concepts.why_it_matters: The recap's L1 key-concept list jumps from Reasoning models (slide 11) to Embeddings (slide 13), so the deck's own slide 12 has no coverage anywhere in the recap even though the concepts record carries it; a learner cannot tell what Part 1 said between those two.

missing_concepts.source_ref: AAPLecture1_LLM_Foundations slide 16 ('Why long chats forget / The hook, answered.'); concepts record entry 'Why long chats forget', slide 16; the hook it answers is slide 2 ('Today we answer it mechanically, not vaguely.')
missing_concepts.why_it_matters: Neither the deck's opening hook (slide 2) nor the slide where the deck says it is answered (slide 16) appears in the recap, so the one narrative thread L1 states for itself is invisible to a learner.

missing_concepts.concept: Mock version history — 'One prompt, three versions.'

missing_concepts.why_it_matters: The recap lists 'Mock version history' only as a topic label in §3 and never states it as a concept, its one-line claim, or that its content is a declared gap; §8 does not list slide 24 among the gaps, so a reader gets neither the concept nor the limitation.

unsupported_claims.claim: Both were detected from the data (850 occurrences of the token across 34 slides) and stripped: 3,696 watermark lines and 112 footers across the four decks.
unsupported_claims.source_ref: No source carries 850. extracted/AAPLecture1_LLM_Foundations/manifest.json records cleaning.watermarkLines 1122 and cleaning.footerDropped 34; evidence/logs/extract-pdf.log records 'watermark fragments:1122 lines removed' and 'footers dropped: 34'. The surrounding figures do reconcile (1122+924+726+924 = 3,696; 34+28+22+28 = 112).
unsupported_claims.note: A specific occurrence count appears in no manifest, log, concepts record or slide file; it is an unsourced number inside a section whose stated purpose is to report only what the data shows.

unsupported_claims.claim: Its findings and the resulting edits are recorded in `output/course_recap_review.json` and `evidence/review/`.
unsupported_claims.source_ref: No such file exists: output/ contains only course_recap.json and course_recap.md, and evidence/review/ contains only course_recap.draft.md. docs/planning.md §11.2 (E6) and §9 place reviewer output at `evidence/review/<deck>.review.json` and `output/reviews/<deck-slug>.review.json`.
unsupported_claims.note: The recap asserts an inspectable review record that is absent and points at a path the project plan does not use, so a reader cannot check the claimed findings or edits.

unsupported_claims.claim: The thread connecting the four decks is that a model is a mechanism, not an oracle.
unsupported_claims.source_ref: No slide in any deck states this framing; the closest source lines are L1 slide 2 'Today we answer it mechanically, not vaguely.' and L3 slide 9 'The model proposes. The harness does.'
unsupported_claims.note: Editorial framing presented as the decks' shared thesis; harmless as commentary but unsourced, in a document that states 'Every claim below is traceable to a slide reference.'

inaccurate_claims.claim: Lecture 4 to RAG on Day 4 (L4 slide 27)
inaccurate_claims.source_ref: AAPLecture4_Inference_Basics slide 27: 'Up next: Day 4 / Today was about how fast an answer comes back. Tomorrow: how to make sure the answer is actually right, using retrieval-augmented generation (RAG).' Slide 1 of the same deck already reads 'DAY 4 · ASTRA · ONLINE SESSION', which the recap repeats in §2.
inaccurate_claims.distortion: Slide 27 is a forward pointer ('Up next', 'Tomorrow'), so it places the RAG session after this deck, not on Day 4. The recap's own §2 table has Day 4 as this deck's day, so as written the sentence puts RAG on the same day as the inference lecture and silently resolves a day-number conflict the source itself contains, without flagging it — as it does flag the L4 part-ordering anomaly.

inaccurate_claims.claim: L1 slide 32's 'Five ideas' and L2 slide 27's 'Five ideas, one answer' are therefore not recoverable from the text layer and are not listed as revision points.
inaccurate_claims.source_ref: extracted/AAPLecture1_LLM_Foundations/slide-32.md line 7 'Five ideas, one answer.'; extracted/AAPLecture2_Prompt_Engineering/slide-27.md line 7 'Five ideas, one answer.'; the L1 concepts record's unavailable_content entry for slide 32 reads "only the running label 'RECAP' and the one-line caption 'Five ideas, one answer.' survived the text layer".
inaccurate_claims.distortion: The quoted line is present verbatim in both text layers; only the individual recap items behind it are unrecoverable. The recap also contradicts itself: §7 lists 'Five ideas, one answer.' (slide 32) as an L1 revision point and §3 lists the same phrase as an L2 topic, then §8 says it is not recoverable and not listed.

inaccurate_claims.claim: Lecture 3: None found in the source as text. Slides 8, 9, 14, 18 and 24 carry interactive or graphical material whose contents are not in the text layer.

Per the L3 concepts record the image-only regions are in fact slides 2–22, so the list also understates the deck-wide gap that §8 describes.

inaccurate_claims.claim: **Not read at all.** L1 slide 33 is a Kahoot quiz slide; L4 slide 28 is an appendix source list; L3 slide 22 and L2 slide 28 are next-up previews. Their contents are not summarised because they are navigational or bibliographic.
inaccurate_claims.source_ref: These four slides were extracted and are text-bearing: L1 slide 33 ('Quiz Time! / Four options, one answer. / ABC / kahoot.com'), L4 slide 28 (529 characters, the largest in any deck, listing seven sources including 'Defeating Nondeterminism in LLM Inference — thinkingmachines.ai' and 'vLLM docs: Parallelism and Scaling · Sarathi-Serve (OSDI 2024) — docs.vllm.ai'), L3 slide 22 and L2 slide 28.
inaccurate_claims.distortion: The heading asserts the slides were not read when their text is present; the L4 appendix is the densest slide in the corpus and two of its entries are mentioned nowhere in the recap. Declining to summarise is defensible; describing the slides as unread is not.
